note: Opened 2026-10-07: the county PDF itself (16 pages), 'Resolution No. 9-2022, Resolution of the Board of County Commissioners of Cherokee County Regulating and Licensing Industrial-Scale Wind Turbine Power Generation Facilities', 'PASSED and APPROVED by the Board of County Commissioners of Cherokee County, Kansas, this 3rd day of October, 2022', effective upon publication. The record's three values match: Sec. 3.C.4.a, 'a distance of 5250 feet between any turbine located in Cherokee County and the nearest property line'; Sec. 3.C.1, 'The maximum turbine height of any wind turbine shall not exceed four hundred forty (440) feet'; Sec. 3.C.3.a, no audible noise above '39 dBA ... during the hours of 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.' at any property line within 5250 feet of the nearest turbine. Differences from the record: it is a resolution, not an ordinance; the 39 dBA limit runs 10 p.m. to 7 a.m., not 'evening'. The source also sets, and the record does not mention: 45 dBA / 55 dBC from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.; a 5 dBA tonal penalty; low-frequency (0.1 to 20 Hz) limits of 50 dB; turbines at least 6 rotor diameters apart; aircraft detection lighting; setbacks of 2 times turbine height from public road rights of way, third-party transmission lines, antennas, communications and water towers, 2,500 feet from cropland that can be aerially sprayed, 5 nautical miles from any airport or landing strip, 3 miles from state wildlife refuges, lakes or rivers, and never closer than 5250 feet to a primary structure; 100 feet of blade clearance; small-scale wind turbines capped at 130 feet with a setback of 3 times turbine height. Night and day noise limits may be waived by a recorded agreement with all landowners within 5250 feet. Removed from the earlier note, which came from search-index text: that it was adopted unanimously and the reference to the commission minutes; the resolution read here shows the date but not the vote, and the minutes were not opened.

Opened 2026-10-08: Washington County (Colorado) Board of County Commissioners Resolution 16-2026, 'A Resolution ... Adopting Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Facilities Zoning Regulations', approved April 14, 2026 after hearings on March 17 and 31, 2026 (pages 1 to 3 of 22). Section 3: 'This resolution shall be in full force and effect upon its passage and approval ending the moratorium for Battery Energy Storage Systems, Resolution 59-2025.' Contradicts the record: the record shows the BESS moratorium as active, but the county ended it on 2026-04-14 and replaced it with permanent regulations requiring a use-by-special-review permit for BESS of 1 MW or more. The earlier moratorium resolutions in the chain (59-2025 and its predecessors) were seen only in search results.
